question: What does the IMD bulletin say about cotton and groundnut pests in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat?
answer:
Task 1: From the Ahmedabad, Gujarat bulletin issued 2026-09-11, for cotton:

Cotton · Squaring/ Flowering/ Boll formation · page 3:
“To prevent an increase in the population of whiteflies and jassids (leafhoppers), do not use synthetic pyrethroid insecticides until the month of November.”

Cotton · Squaring/ Flowering/ Boll formation · page 3:
“Sucking pest infestation in cotton at initial stage can be controlled by spraying 500 g of neem seed kernel extract (5% NSKE) or 50 ml of neem oil or a neem-based insecticide by mixing 10 ml (5 EC) to 50 ml (0.03 EC) in 10 litres of water. If the infestation is severe, spray Flonicamid 50 WG with 3 g or Diafenthiuron 50 WP with 10 g or Dinotefuran 20 SG with 3 g by mixing the recommended quantity in 10 litres of water.”

Context from the same bulletin edition follows. These are separate source sections, not crop-specific matches or verified current official warnings. Printed warning dates and conditions are preserved; bulletin forecast dates do not extend their validity.

Weather summary · page 1:
“As per weather forecast received from Meteorological Centre, Ahmedabad probability of cloudy sky during next five days with light rainfall on 12-09-2026, 13-09-2026, 16-09-2026; moderate rainfall on 14-09-2026 and 15-09-2026 at isolated places very likely. Extended Range Forecast: Maximum temperature, minimum temperature likely to be normal and rainfall likely to be below normal during subsequent week 16-09-2026 to 22-09-2026 in Gujarat region. Note: The above given weather forecast is average situation for whole district, so it should not applicable for one place.”

General advice · page 2:
“Undertake interculturing and weeding operations to conserve moisture in standing monsoon crops and apply need based light irrigation by considering weather and soil moisture condition in standing crops. Application of fertilizer or top dressing should undertake only under optimum soil moisture condition in standing crops. Farmers are advised to download MEGHDOOT mobile application for acquiring information regarding Agromet Advisory in Gujarati language. Click on following link to download this application user: https://play,google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.aas.meghdoot”

These are original English source excerpts, including their conditions. The bulletin is district guidance; it has not been validated for your individual field.

Task 2: From the Ahmedabad, Gujarat bulletin issued 2026-09-11, for groundnut:

Groundnut · Flowering/ Pod formation · page 3:
“White grubs in groundnut can be controlled by spraying Chlorpyrifos 20 EC with 4 litres per hectare through drip irrigation or along with irrigation. If irrigation is not being given but intermittent rainfall is occurring, prepare the insecticide solution in a spray pump, remove the nozzle and apply the solution directly into the furrows in the required quantity.”

Groundnut · Flowering/ Pod formation · page 3:
“Leaf-eating caterpillar (Spodoptera) in groundnut can be controlled by installing one light trap per hectare in the affected area and destroy the adult moths and leaf- eating caterpillar moths attracted to the trap.”

Groundnut · Flowering/ Pod formation · page 3:
“Leaf-eating caterpillar (Spodoptera) in groundnut can be controlled by installing pheromone traps with 40 traps per hectare on a community basis to keep the pest population under control. At the initial stage of infestation, spray either neem seed kernel powder extract at 500 g (5% extract) or a neem-based insecticide at 20 ml (1 EC) to 40 ml (0.15 EC) mixed in 10 litres of water. If the infestation becomes severe, spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC at 3 ml or Flubendiamide 20 WG at 6 g or Thiamethoxam 12.6% + Lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% ZC at 3 ml 10 litres of water.”
